recommendation: Keep the audit commit and do not reintroduce a tooling or source restriction for nested complex-extension parts marked Is-Modifier=true unless a new work-group decision changes the post-FHIR-8548 model.
issue_request: FHIR-8549 was a Published/Persuasive DSTU1 FHIR-core extensibility issue asking tooling to reject extension definitions whose nested child elements were flagged isModifier=Y until FHIR decided extensions could contain modifiers.
initial_application: The issue was historically applied by commit 467588e0b14b4d1a761ab22b4424968836f1e49f, whose subject references #8549 and whose git-svn revision matches the Jira comment. That old tooling rejection is no longer present in the current checkout.
additional_context: FHIR-8548 later made the policy decision anticipated by FHIR-8549, allowing components of complex extensions to be marked isModifier while requiring them to be conveyed using extension rather than modifierExtension. FHIR-11036, FHIR-18352, and FHIR-37903 later refined the same guidance and are already represented on the combined branch.
reconciliation: Published an empty audit commit. The current active source/extensibility.html, which is in build scope via source/fhir.ini, already reflects the later rule and should not be changed to restore the obsolete FHIR-8549 rejection.
